summary:
1. Summary
Space Explorers is an interactive educational website free for everyone, which brings the stories of space hardware by which people have reached other worlds – and the science these machines have made possible – to life. The project is based on the left-behind or ongoing deep space travels of the Surveyor 3, Lunar Roving Vehicle, Viking 1, Sojourner, Opportunity, Ingenuity, Voyager 1 and Pioneer 10. Different worlds will be presented and visitors will get to know the hardware through illustrated characters, hear stories being read to them, have to solve age-suitable quizzes, play space games and do gravity experiments. The project not only identifies the issue of the “Abandoned but Not Forgotten”, but it also addresses it by converting silent hardware into stories for young space enthusiasts. It is important because it helps kids realise that the space missions have an impact on us even after hardware has ceased working.
details:
Space Explorers: Abandoned but Not Forgotten

1. Project Overview: How and What Is It Doing?

Space Explorers: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive, browser-based educational platform designed for school-age space enthusiasts. It aims to bring the stories of historic and abandoned space hardware back to life by transforming them into engaging digital learning experiences.

Visitors are immersed in different space environments where they discover spacecraft, scientific instruments, and exploration equipment through illustrated characters, storytelling, interesting facts, quizzes, games, and interactive experiments.

The website features 27 Space Explorers, with particular emphasis on nine that are especially relevant to the NASA Space Apps Challenge:

  • Surveyor 3
  • Lunar Roving Vehicle
  • Lunar Laser Reflectors
  • Viking 1 Lander
  • Sojourner
  • Opportunity
  • Ingenuity
  • Voyager 1
  • Pioneer 10

Each explorer is presented through an illustrated character, a short story, educational facts, and a quiz question. This approach gives historic space equipment a recognizable identity and makes its scientific contributions easier for children to understand.

Interactive Storytelling

The project also features an astronaut-themed storytelling experience with illustrated animal characters. On the Moon and Mars pages, visitors can choose an astronaut or a Mars practice crew member and listen to their stories narrated directly by the browser.

The storytelling experience incorporates animated mouth movements, synchronized captions, and an audio-level visualizer. These features create a more immersive experience while helping children follow the narration visually and through audio.

Interactive Games and Experiments

The learning experience is further supported by interactive games and science experiments:

  • Planet Hopper: A 2D space platformer that allows players to explore and navigate through space-themed environments.
  • UFO Stomp 3D: An immersive 3D arena game featuring 27 levels.
  • Gravity Room: An interactive simulation demonstrating the effects of gravity on Earth, the Moon, Mars, and Jupiter, allowing students to explore how gravity differs across celestial bodies.

These activities encourage children to move beyond reading information and actively engage with scientific concepts through exploration and experimentation.

2. How Does It Address the NASA Challenge?

The central idea behind Abandoned but Not Forgotten is that the end of a space mission does not mean the end of its educational or historical value.

Spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space represent important achievements in human exploration. However, their stories and contributions may be unfamiliar to younger generations.

Space Explorers addresses this gap by turning these pieces of historic space hardware into interactive educational characters.

Instead of simply displaying information about abandoned equipment, the platform introduces children to the missions, their purposes, their discoveries, and the people and technology behind them.

By presenting these explorers through stories, illustrations, quizzes, and interactive activities, the project helps preserve their legacy while making space history accessible to a younger audience.

The platform transforms the idea of abandoned space hardware from something forgotten into an opportunity for curiosity, discovery, and learning.

3. Benefits and Educational Value

Space science becomes more accessible and engaging for children by combining storytelling, games, quizzes, animations, audio, and interactive simulations.

Instead of simply consuming facts about historic space equipment, students can interact with the information, participate in activities, and test their understanding through quizzes and experiments.

The platform provides several educational benefits:

  • Space exploration awareness: Introduces children to historic missions, spacecraft, rovers, and scientific instruments.
  • Scientific understanding: Helps explain concepts such as gravity and planetary environments through interactive demonstrations.
  • Learning through play: Uses games and challenges to reinforce scientific concepts in an enjoyable way.
  • Knowledge retention: Combines visual storytelling, narration, quizzes, and practical interaction to make information more memorable.
  • Independent exploration: Allows children to explore different space environments and learning activities at their own pace.

The age-adaptive learning experience is particularly valuable because the website targets children approximately 6–15 years old. Stories and quizzes vary according to the selected age group, helping accommodate different reading abilities and learning levels.

4. Intended Impact

The primary goal is to teach young learners that space hardware can continue to hold scientific, historical, and educational value long after its original mission has ended.

The project aims to develop curiosity about space exploration while introducing children to important scientific and technological concepts.

Through the platform, students can learn:

  • How gravity varies between planets and moons.
  • How robotic spacecraft and scientific instruments contribute to space exploration.
  • How real people design, develop, and operate space missions.
  • Why engineering, technology, research, and teamwork are essential to exploring space.
  • How historic missions continue to contribute to scientific knowledge and inspire future discoveries.

The intended long-term impact is to encourage children to develop an interest in science, technology, engineering, and space exploration while understanding the importance of preserving the legacy of past missions.

The Space Explorers may have been abandoned, but their stories, discoveries, and educational value are not forgotten.

5. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware and Software

The project was developed as a single-page, browser-based web application using the following technologies:

Programming Languages and Frameworks

  • HTML
  • CSS
  • JavaScript
  • Tailwind CSS (used for Planet Hopper)

Web Technologies and Features

  • Web Audio API: Used for generating live sound effects.
  • Browser-based Text-to-Speech: Provides narration and storytelling without requiring a separate audio application.
  • JavaScript: Powers interactive website features, games, and simulations.
  • AI-generated illustrations: Used to create visual characters and enhance the storytelling experience.

Software and Requirements

  • A JavaScript-enabled web browser, such as Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, or Opera.
  • An internet connection to access the website.

The 3D game and Gravity Room are rendered directly inside the browser, while the two other games are integrated into the website and can be played without navigating away from the platform.

The project does not require any physical hardware. It is primarily a software-based educational solution accessible through a web browser, making it easier for students to explore the experience using commonly available devices.

6. How Is the Project Innovative?

The creativity of Space Explorers lies in combining space history, interactive storytelling, and gaming into a unified educational experience.

Rather than presenting abandoned spacecraft as forgotten relics, the project gives them illustrated personalities and individual stories. Visitors can explore their missions, learn interesting facts, listen to narrated stories, answer questions, and play games related to space science.

Several elements distinguish the project:

1. Bringing Abandoned Hardware to Life

Historic space equipment is presented through illustrated characters and storytelling, helping children connect with missions and understand their scientific contributions.

2. Age-Adaptive Learning

Stories and quizzes vary according to the visitor's selected age group, making the platform suitable for children with different reading abilities and levels of understanding.

3. Learning Through Interaction

Games and interactive experiments allow students to explore scientific concepts rather than simply reading about them.

4. Integrated Multimedia Experience

The combination of narration, captions, animated characters, audio, illustrations, and interactive simulations creates multiple ways for children to engage with educational content.

5. Accessible Browser-Based Learning

The platform brings its educational content and interactive activities together in one browser-based experience without requiring specialized physical hardware or user accounts.

By combining historical space missions with modern interactive technology, Space Explorers demonstrates how abandoned space hardware can continue to educate and inspire future generations.

7. Design Considerations and Challenges Addressed

Throughout development, the team considered several important factors to create an engaging and accessible learning experience.

  • Young target audience: Designing an experience suitable for children with different levels of understanding.
  • Engaging education: Making space science enjoyable through games, storytelling, and interactive activities rather than relying entirely on reading.
  • Different learning abilities: Accommodating the reading and learning differences of children aged 6–15 through age-adaptive content.
  • Accessibility: Providing narration, captions, and read-aloud options to support different learning preferences.
  • Responsive design: Creating navigation and layouts that adapt to different screen sizes and devices.
  • Dark and Light Themes: Offering theme options to improve the visual experience and readability.
  • Scientific accuracy: Considering the accuracy of mission facts, educational content, and quiz questions.
  • Responsible use of AI: Using AI-generated illustrations and narration appropriately.
  • Attribution: Ensuring appropriate acknowledgment and citation of external resources and creative work.
  • Privacy: Keeping the platform free from user accounts, advertisements, and tracking mechanisms.

These considerations helped shape the project into an educational experience that prioritizes accessibility, engagement, age suitability, and responsible technology use.

8. Use of AI Tools

AI tools were used throughout the research, development, and testing process to support different aspects of the project.

  • ChatGPT: Used for research assistance, gathering and organizing information, refining educational content, and testing different website features and functionalities.
  • Claude: Used as a coding assistant to support code development, implementation, debugging, and improvements to website functionality.
  • Flow AI: Used to create animations and background music, enhancing the website's visual appeal and overall audio experience.

These tools supported the development process, while the project concept, feature selection, integration, testing, and overall implementation were guided and carried out by the team.

Space Explorers: Abandoned but Not Forgotten

Because a mission may end, but its legacy can continue to inspire generations of explorers.
